gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Jackery's HomePower 1000 v2 (23.4 lb) does charge from solar: it has two 200 W DC ports, 400 W in total, which is the same layout as the Explorer 1000 v2. Several results do agree it is the lighter unit, but ChatGPT's "no solar" caveat is wrong. None of them puts each maker's solar figure on the same footing either: the Explorer's 400 W needs two panels on two ports at 200 W each, and the Anker C1000 Gen 2 takes only 8.2 A below 29 V, so its 600 W needs a high-voltage panel array.
standout_why: I compared against backup-power.org (cited), keeplights.com (cited), amphourly.com (cited), solarpowerauditor.com camping (cited), faq.jackery.com (cited) and our own dealectric page. Cycle life is already put on the same basis elsewhere: backup-power.org, keeplights and amphourly all note that Jackery rates 4,000 cycles to 70% while the others rate to 80%. Backup-power.org and keeplights also note the fast-charge modes you switch on in the app. Every rival lists total solar watts only. For Jackery and Anker, keeplights, amphourly, solarpowerauditor and backup-power.org all say 'voltage not stated' or 'per-port not stated'. Our page says HomePower 1000 v2 solar is 'none listed', and every ChatGPT answer repeated that caveat to keep the Explorer as the pick. The Jackery FAQ gives the per-port limits, but no answer used them.
decides: This changes the pick. If the HomePower 1000 v2 has 400 W of solar on two 200 W DC ports, it is the lightest solar-capable 1 kWh LiFePO4 unit at 23.4 lb, 0.4 lb under the Explorer 1000 v2's 23.8 lb. The Explorer's lead in Wh per lb rests on its 1,070 Wh rating. Jackery's own blog listing shows it at 1,024 Wh, which works out to 43.0 Wh/lb against the HomePower's 43.8. Normalising solar also changes the runner-up advice. With one panel of about 20 V Vmp, the Explorer can take up to 200 W, while the Anker C1000 Gen 2 is held to about 164 W by its 8.2 A limit. The Anker's 600 W only arrives at 29–60 V, which in practice means several panels in series. Weight to the HomePower, but this needs a check on Jackery's own US page before it goes live.
